name: CycloProp: Advanced UAV Propulsion Challenge
desc: A national, MeitY-funded challenge to design a build-ready cycloidal rotor module for drones, taking teams from concept to a CAE-supported detailed design under expert mentorship.
about: CycloProp is Grand Challenge  of the PUSHPAK Grand Challenge 2026, a national innovation challenge under the PUSHPAK: National Mission on Drone Technology, funded by MeitY, Government of India, and hosted by IIT Bombay. Unlike a conventional hackathon or idea competition, this challenge takes promising technical concepts through evaluation, mentoring, and deployment-oriented development. Teams work with researchers, domain experts, and industry mentors to design an indigenous cycloidal rotor module for drone applications, targeting at least 10 N thrust and a thrust-to-weight ratio greater than 2.5. The goal isn't immediate prototype fabrication, but identifying strong, build-ready cyclorotor designs. Selected winning teams get invited to a post-challenge Prototype Development Support Programme to bridge the gap between innovation and real-world deployment.
structure:
"The Grand Challenge runs about 4 months across three stages, ending with final presentations at Techfest, IIT Bombay, in December 2026.

Eligibility: Open to academic institutions, faculty-led student teams, startups, MSMEs, and academia-startup-industry consortia with expertise in UAVs, rotorcraft, aerodynamics, robotics, controls, or mechanical design.

Team size: Up to 5 members per team.

Objective: Teams work on a single objective, the CAE-supported design of an indigenous cycloidal rotor module for drone applications, targeting at least 10 N thrust and a thrust-to-weight ratio greater than 2.5.

Stage 1 - Preliminary Design Submission
Teams get about a month to submit a preliminary cyclorotor design covering configuration, rotor sizing, blade-pitch concept, estimated thrust and weight, and a manufacturing approach. No funding at this stage; up to 15 teams qualify and receive INR 1 Lakh each.

Stage 2 - Detailed Design Development
Over about two months, shortlisted teams build a complete, CAE-supported design package: CAD model, kinematic and aerodynamic analysis, structural assessment, material selection, and a build-and-test plan. Up to 10 teams advance to the finale with travel and accommodation support.

Stage 3 - Grand Challenge Finale
Finalists present and defend their detailed design before the evaluation committee at Techfest, IIT Bombay, with a technical viva. Up to 5 winning teams are selected and considered for further funding, mentoring, and resources in the post-challenge Prototype Development Support Programme."

rules:
Participants must register on the official Techfest website (techfest.org > Competitions > PUSHPAK Grand Challenge) before taking part.
All Stage 1 and Stage 2 submissions must be made via email to pushpak_gc2026@aero.iitb.ac.in; no submission links or forms are used.
No financial support is provided at Stage 1; funding and support begin only for teams shortlisted into Stage 2 and beyond.
The process for disbursement of prize money and support will be communicated at a later stage; teams are advised to regularly check the official website and their registered email for updates.
The decision of the organizing team and evaluation committee shall be treated as final and binding on all.
Travel or participation support for finalist teams is subject to approved budget norms and IIT Bombay's guidelines, to be shared at a later stage.
faq:
Q: Who can participate?
A:Academic institutions, faculty-led student teams, startups, MSMEs, and academia-startup-industry consortia working in UAVs, rotorcraft, aerodynamics, robotics, controls, or mechanical design.

Q: What's the team size?
A:Up to 5 members per team.

Q: What are the two objectives, and can we attempt both?
A:The PS only lays out one stated objective, the CAE-supported design of an indigenous cycloidal rotor module. Worth confirming with the team if a second objective exists that isn't reflected in this document, before this FAQ goes out.

Q: Is this a one-shot competition or a staged programme?
A:It's a staged programme, not a one-shot competition. Teams move through three stages, preliminary design, detailed design development, and the Grand Finale, with shortlisting and funding support at each stage, followed by a post-challenge Prototype Development Support Programme for winning teams.

Q: How do we submit our proposals?
A:Entirely via email to pushpak_gc2026@aero.iitb.ac.in. There are no submission links or forms; every stage is handled through email correspondence.


Q: What happens after the Grand Finale for winning teams?
A:Up to 5 winning teams are invited into a dedicated Prototype Development Support Programme starting December 2026, bridging their prototype toward real-world deployment with further funding, mentoring, and access to resources.

Q: What is the evaluation criteria?
A:Scored across nine weighted criteria, covering thrust feasibility, thrust-to-weight ratio, kinematic design, aerodynamic analysis, structural design, manufacturability, CAD quality, and presentation.

Q: Who are the faculty mentors guiding this Grand Challenge?
A:Prof. Arnab Maity, Aerospace Engineering, IIT Bombay, whose expertise spans autonomous flight systems, UAV and drone technologies, and guidance and control; and Dr. Dhwanil Shukla, Department of Aerospace Engineering, IIT Bombay, whose research focuses on rotorcraft design, low-speed aerodynamics, and experimental flow-diagnostic techniques.
